corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-139 | **PERFORM statement — whether location information is available when the LOCATION phrase is not specified**, §14.9.28.4 GR14 (through §7.3.25.4 GR7), required + documented | **Not available.** An exception-checking PERFORM (Format 3, `PERFORM … WHEN exception-name …  END-PERFORM`) enables the exception conditions its WHEN phrases name over imperative-statement-1 through an implicit TURN directive (§14.9.28.4 GR14), and that implicit directive carries LOCATION exactly when the PERFORM writes `WITH LOCATION`. Without it COBOL.NET saves no location information for a condition raised there — the same determination as the explicit `>>TURN` directive (item 204), so neither route yields location data the other withholds. Consequence inside the WHEN handler and after the PERFORM: `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION` returns one alphanumeric space, `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` one national space and `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT` 63 spaces, while `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS` still names the condition. With `PERFORM WITH LOCATION` the full location is produced — e.g. `PL; MAIN-P; 12` and statement `RAISE`. ⛔ **An explicit TURN that already enables the name wins, in both directions:** §14.9.28.4 GR14 assumes the implicit TURN only "if checking … is not enabled for imperative-statement-1 by a TURN directive", so when a `>>TURN … CHECKING ON` in force before the PERFORM already enables a name its WHEN phrase lists, no implicit directive is assumed for that name and THAT directive's LOCATION setting governs — under `>>TURN EC-USER-X1 CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` a PERFORM without LOCATION still yields `PL2; MAIN-P; 7`, and under `>>TURN EC-USER-X1 CHECKING ON` (no LOCATION) a `PERFORM WITH LOCATION` yields one space. The LOCATION flag travels on `BoundExceptionPerform.WithLocation` into `TurnState.WithImplicitEnable`. COBOL 2023 only (Format 3 PERFORM is COBOLNET0900 in earlier editions). | `conformance:2023/l1_exception_no_location_arms`; `conformance:2023/exception_statement_ambient` |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-153 | **Record locking — the default mode when the user specifies none**, §12.4.5.9.4 GR1 b) 2., required + documented | **No record locking** — the third option GR1 b) 2. names. A file connector whose file control entry has neither a LOCK MODE clause nor a SHARING clause, opened by an OPEN with no SHARING phrase, SETS NO RECORD LOCKS: a READ does not lock, and an explicit `WITH LOCK` phrase on its I-O statements obtains nothing (`FileRegistry.ImplementorDefaultShare`, lock mode `FileLockMode.None`). It still RESPECTS other connectors' locks, because §9.1.16 makes a locked record inaccessible to every other file connector: its READ, REWRITE and DELETE of a record another connector has locked are refused with I-O status `51`, and READ … IGNORING LOCK reads it. Example (that two clause-less connectors can have the file open at the same time is the DEFAULT SHARING MODE, item 131, which is not yet determined — kb/Work PB322; the example shows the lock behaviour only): two such connectors on one relative file — A `READ … WITH LOCK` record 1 (`00`), B READs and REWRITEs record 1 (`00`, `00`); a third connector with `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC` READs record 1 and locks it, and B's next READ of record 1 is `51`. COBOL 2002 and later. | `conformance:2002/pb669_lock_visibility_plain_connector` |
